Statehouse wins give Democrats new power to push clean energy

=== MULTI-SOURCE TOPIC CLUSTER: Statehouse wins give Democrats new power to push clean energy ===

[Source 1 — arstechnica.visitlink.me (Bias: Independent / Unrated)] (URL: https://arstechnica.visitlink.me/xIq8aV):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Statehouse wins give Democrats new power to push clean energy

Democrats erased the GOP’s trifecta edge and gained new power over energy policy.

Actual Article Body:
Democrats erased the GOP’s trifecta edge and gained new power over energy policy.

Before Tuesday’s election, Republicans held more governorships and state legislative seats than Democrats, along with an advantage in state trifectas—unified control of the governor’s office and both chambers of the legislature.

That advantage has disappeared, clearing the path for more climate and clean energy legislation, according to analysts and advocates.

Democrats swept the vast majority of competitive races at the state level, flipping control of governors’ offices from Republicans in Georgia, Iowa, Ohio, Nevada, and Texas.

Democrats have a 29-19 edge in governorships, with Kansas too close to call and Alaska likely to take a while to declare a winner.

The party is on track for a net gain of hundreds of legislative seats, potentially giving it control of more nationwide than Republicans for the first time in more than a decade. Going into the election, Republicans had 4,072 seats and Democrats held 3,257, according to MultiState, a research and lobbying firm. Democrats had a net gain of more than 350 seats on Tuesday and are likely to add several hundred more as results continue to be tabulated, according to MultiState.

Democrats won five new trifectas: Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin, with Arizona likely to be the sixth once officials finish counting. Those additions would give the party 22 trifectas, with Republicans holding unified control in 18 states and nine with split control. Kansas is yet to be determined.

Republicans lost trifectas in Iowa, Georgia, Texas, New Hampshire, and Ohio. Before the election, Republicans had trifectas in 23 states, Democrats had 16, and 11 were under split control.

The implications for climate and energy policy are likely to be profound, said Caroline Spears, executive director of Climate Cabinet, an advocacy group.

“In the states, we had a generational political window shift to make people’s lives better, to lower costs, and to lower climate pollution at the same time,” she said in a conference call.

This was the “affordability election” with concerns about inflation and high energy prices, she said.

Newly elected lawmakers will enter office with energy policy proposals to address voter concerns, she...

[Source 2 — www.motherjones.com (Bias: Left)] (URL: https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2026/11/democrats-congress-corruption-henry-cuellar-trump-pardon-investigation-appropriations/):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Democrats are ready to investigate corruption—with one exception

Rep. Henry Cuellar won a Trump pardon and beat a gerrymander. Will his colleagues protect him?

Actual Article Body:
Mother Jones illustration; om Williams/CQ-Roll Call/Getty

Voters threw Republicans out of office on Tuesday by astounding margins, in large part due to disgust with Donald Trump’s extensively documented corruption. And Democrats have vowed to follow that mandate and “hold those who are enriching themselves through corruption at taxpayers’ expense accountable,” as Rep. Katherine Clark (D-Mass.), who is expected to become House Majority Leader, said Wednesday.

Democrats have outlined investigative plans that run the gamut from Trump family crypto schemes to funding for Trump’s vanity projects to his use of pardons to help political allies and campaign donors.

But one place congressional Dems do not appear eager to look is within their own caucus. Rep. Henry Cuellar (D-Texas) was charged by federal prosecutors in 2024 with taking a combined total of around $600,000 in bribes from an oil company controlled by the government of Azerbaijan and from a bank headquartered in...

[Source 3 — www.washingtonexaminer.com (Bias: Right / Conservative)] (URL: https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/campaigns/presidential/4795152/democrats-2028-ambitions-flock-clyburn-midterms/):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Democrats with 2028 ambitions flock to Clyburn after midterm elections

Rep. Jim Clyburn (D-SC) has become the man of the hour for Democrats looking to launch a 2028 presidential bid, as he revealed that several lawmakers have reached out to him after the party swept up a House and Senate majority in the midterm elections. Clyburn told Politico that he received phone calls from four […]

Actual Article Body:
Rep. Jim Clyburn (D-SC) has become the man of the hour for Democrats looking to launch a 2028 presidential bid, as he revealed that several lawmakers have reached out to him after the party swept up a House  and Senate majority in the midterm elections.

Clyburn told Politico that he received phone calls from four individuals weighing a presidential bid as they try to woo the South Carolina heavyweight, with the state set to hold the first 2028 presidential primary.
